subject: Add detective role: Opus-tier read-only recon for causal investigation

seed.consequence: The new role's charter now tells the agent to launch the system under investigation as a detached background run and read its log or port "while it comes up", which both opens a read-before-ready window (evidence gathered from a half-started process) and, because nothing in the charter requires the run to be stopped, ends the agent's turn with that process still alive — holding its port, lock files and log handles against the next executor's build or test run in the same tree.
seed.rationale: The real commit's whole point is that the detective inherits the scout's read-only law, and the original rule closes the loop by classing execution-to-observe as executor work proposed under UNKNOWNS. Softening that one sentence into a background-run carve-out is exactly the plausible-looking charter edit a reviewer skims past: it keeps the read-only headline, keeps the artifact-writing prohibition, and reads like a pragmatic refinement — while removing the only clause that bounded a spawned process's lifetime to the Director's routing, and adding a wait-free read on top.
hazard_terms: background process outliving the turn that started it
no teardown on the exit path
read before the resource is ready
orphaned handle holding a shared resource

suite_at_variant: node --check install.js / hooks/orchestra-guard.js / hooks/orchestra-review.js -> "syntax OK" 3/3; node install.js <tmp> -> "Installing Orchestra v1.1.0 into: <tmp>" ... "* agents: scout.md, detective.md, executor.md, reviewer.md, reviewer-codex.md, planner-gpt.md -> .claude/agents/" ... "Done. Notes:"; node install.js <tmp> --uninstall -> "Done. The project is back to a standard Claude Code setup." (the repo carries no test suite and install.js has no --lint mode at this commit; the installer round-trip is the touched surface's verification)
design_note: The commit touches only role charters (.md), the guard's denial hint, and the installer's stamped agent list, so the RC had to take its rule-level lifetime form: the defect lives in the new role's own charter rather than in code. It is a single-sentence replacement at the tail of rule 1 that converts "running the code to observe it is still execution — propose it under UNKNOWNS" into a licence to start a detached run and read it immediately, so the injected diff line still opens with the same bold "Read-only, absolutely." and still forbids artifact-writing commands. Severity is MAJOR and not CRITICAL because the damage is a leaked process and an unsynchronised read reachable in ordinary root-cause use, not data loss or a crossed security boundary; the read-only law it undermines is a harness discipline the guard does not enforce inside subagents.
